device.description: Dual 12-bit multiplying current-output DAC with 24-bit serial interface, update pins and asynchronous clear
device.note: dac7800.pdf (SBAS005B) p.2 electrical (VDD 4.5-5.5 V), p.3 pin configuration and logic truth table, p.4 data input format and timing

registers.name: INB
registers.note: shift-register bits 0-11 (DAC B, Bit 0 = MSB, clocked in first)

registers.name: DACA
registers.note: DAC A register (UPD A low with CS low)

registers.name: DACB
registers.note: DAC B register (UPD B low with CS low)

commands.name: Shift 24 bits
commands.note: data clocked in on CLK falling while CS is low, MSB of DAC B first, DAC A last (p.4)

pages: p.2 (VDD), p.3 (pins, truth table: CLK falling edge, CLR async), p.4 (data input sequence, timing)
notModeled: analog: multiplying current outputs IOUT A/B, reference inputs VREF A/B, feedback resistors RFB A/B
power-on register contents are not given (the datasheet suggests CLR for power-on reset); 0 used
separate update pins: UPD A loads DAC A and UPD B loads DAC B (each low with CS low); the schema has one LDAC pin, so UPD A (level, active low) updates both DACs and UPD B is not modeled
UPD is only effective while CS is low (truth table); the model updates whenever UPD A is low
the shift register keeps shifting past 24 bits (the last 24 bits count); the model takes the first 24 bits of a CS-low period
CLR also clears the shift register (all register contents set to 0)
variants: DAC7800 (serial), DAC7801 (8+4-bit parallel, double-buffered) and DAC7802 (12-bit parallel, single-buffered) share dac7800.pdf; own spec files. The DAC7800 is a 16-pin part; skeleton packages DW (SOIC-16W) and N (PDIP-16) share one pin numbering.
